project.description: A tiny frog. An unfair world. One more try. Procedurally generated arcade chaos, built in a week.

sections.title: Simple rules. Infinite trouble.
sections.intro:
An arcade world
that won’t sit still.

blocks.text: **FaraFrog: Devil Game** is a week-long project built around a simple question: how much variety can you get from a few procedural rules? The obstacles change with every level. The goal stays simple: get through it, fast.

blocks.alt: FaraFrog animated title screen with the frog and Devil Game logo
blocks.caption: FaraFrog: Devil Game — the original title-screen animation.

sections.title: Making room for the unexpected
sections.intro:
A random walk.
A very real challenge.

blocks.text: Level generation starts with a **weighted random walk**, with a random range of turns. The first tile at the bottom becomes the spawn; the last tile at the top becomes the exit. The remaining space is filled from a pool of obstacle tiles.

**Rocket tiles** pick a random floor tile, place a marker, and fire when the player triggers it.
**Spinning saws** orbit their tile at a randomly chosen distance.
**Paired saw tiles** create a traversing saw when a line between them crosses the path.
**Keys and locks** add a lock at the exit for each key. Keys that are not adjacent to the path are removed.

The rules deliberately leave room for difficult, sometimes unfair levels. One important safeguard: no shooting tiles within three tiles of spawn, so there is at least one safe place to evade the projectiles.

blocks.alt: FaraFrog level showing a narrow path, saws, projectile tiles and the player frog
blocks.caption: The generated path and obstacle tiles in a playable level.

blocks.text: The score encourages fast completion. The multiplier starts at **×1.5** and decreases by **0.1 each second**. Starting points scale with the number and type of obstacles.

Unlock a door: **+250**
A rift in the level: **+888**
Each saw: **+100**
Each triggered explosion: **+50**
Party hats: **+1,000**, applied after the multiplier
